items.name: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
items.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
items.description: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8+

items.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
items.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains. items.name: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
items.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
items.description: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. items.name: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.description: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this supervision with dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher equipped with an evidence-centered visual view. items.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
items.description: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. items.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
items.description: In this paper, we systematically investigate the mechanisms, scaling behavior, and generalization of physical Recursive self-improvement. We introduce PhysRSI-eval to quantify physical RSI through a five-axis metric: First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency, Success, Budget and Improvement from failure. items.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
items.description: Long-horizon agents must learn heterogeneous capabilities from interleaved trajectories. Updating shared parameters to learn new capabilities can degrade previously acquired ones, resulting in catastrophic forgetting. items.name: Train An Imaginative Agent
items.title: Train An Imaginative Agent
items.description: A seemingly reasonable push in Sokoban can make the puzzle unsolvable. To avoid such mistakes, an agent has to anticipate the consequences of its actions before execution, especially when feedback from the real environment is sparse or actions are irreversible. We introduce Agentic Imagination (Agima), a training framework that trains an agent to imagine before acting, i.e. to be imaginative. items.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
items.description: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. This has the great appeal that it allows agents to plan and simulate a course of actions with the help of a world model. For these uses to be reliable, however, the learned dynamics must behave well beyond the specific state-action combinations observed in expert rollouts. items.name: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
items.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
items.description: Systems that combine several large language models (LLMs) often use one context for many questions. When the context is passed between models as text, the receiving model processes all of its tokens again for every question. Avoiding this cost requires a context representation that is compact, reusable across questions, and readable by a different LLM. items.name: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
items.title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
items.description: Bilevel optimization provides a framework for machine learning tasks such as hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning. Existing Newton-based bilevel methods typically rely on the classical hypergradient formula, which is generally unavailable when lower-level solutions are nonunique and the lower-level Hessian is singular. items.name: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
items.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
items.description: LLM agents that compute the right answer can still answer wrongly. Agent harnesses increasingly keep long tool outputs out of the context window, saving them to files that the agent searches or reads on demand. We ask where this costs accuracy with a real scientific tool: PHREEQC, a widely used geochemistry simulator from the USGS, whose reports reach 846.8k characters and whose determinism lets every printed value be traced. Agents use it to answer 158 execution-verified multiple-choice items.

items.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
items.description: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. items.name: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
items.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
items.description: Machine learning is widely regarded as a promising application in which quantum computing could offer a computational advantage. However, general quantum machine learning models with provable guarantees on performance, trainability, and efficient inference remain limited. items.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures
items.description: Many modern language models have adopted hybrid architectures that incorporate both linear-time recurrence and softmax attention. items.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
items.description: Frontier agents retrieve structural metadata well and compute geometry from coordinates less reliably. We ask how much of a benchmark score reflects that gap and how much reflects the evaluation configuration around the model. We study ProteinGeoBench, a suite of 131 protein-structure tasks, using 4,249 rollouts from four frontier models and 4,486 further trials across 26 models. items.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
items.description: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. items.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression
items.description: Context compression improves long-context efficiency but may introduce faithfulness issues through an information bottleneck. Existing evaluations rely on QA metrics, but a reader can still answer correctly from an unfaithful compression, so these metrics underestimate such loss. items.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
items.description: Beyond basic tool use and coding skills, effectively incorporating visual references into agentic generation is equally essential for applying AI agents to real-world productivity tasks. items.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
items.description: Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information. items.title: SpecMRL: Redesign Matryoshka Representation Learning within Parametric Spectrum
items.description: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) is designed to support flexible representation sizes by jointly optimizing nested prefixes. items.title: AfriBED: a Speech Recognition Bias Evaluation Dataset for Low Resource African Languages
items.description: Despite advancements in automatic speech recognition systems (ASR), current systems exhibit speaker-attribute bias, i.e., their speech recognition performance is biased against certain speakers based on their demographic attributes such as gender, accents, and speaker type. items.title: ASTOR: Benchmarking and Improving Autoformulation for Soft-Constraint Optimization with a Formal Grammar

items.description: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. items.title: Safety Mid-Training: Internalizing LLM Safety as a Foundational Capability
items.description: Safety alignment for large language models (LLMs) is primarily performed during post-training, while recent work has also begun incorporating safety data into pre-training. items.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
items.description: Brain encoding models aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones. items.title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
items.description: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. items.title: Learning to Refer: Inference-Time Collaboration in Decentralized Federated Learning
items.description: In decentralized federated learning, heterogeneous clients may develop complementary expertise, yet each query is typically evaluated only by the client where it arrives.
